chunks: And Ali ibn Muhammad al-Husayni wrote to him that, 'A cousin of mine bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf with fifteen dinars in every year, but it does not suffice, so what are your orders regarding that?' So he wrote: 'He should make two Hajjs to be regarded as one Hajj, Allah is Knowing of that.'

key_terms.حَجَّ عَنْهُ: Hajj performed on behalf of another

ai.seo_question: How is insufficient funds for Hajj handled in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of *taqdir* (proportional valuation) in Shia jurisprudence, where the Imam clarifies that the fixed annual bequest of fifteen dinars, though insufficient for a single Hajj, accumulates to cover the cost of two pilgrimages. By combining these funds, the deceased is credited with two Hajjs, demonstrating the flexibility of financial bequests (*wasiyyah*) in fulfilling religious obligations. This ruling underscores the scholarly emphasis on maximizing spiritual benefit for the deceased through practical financial management.
